criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear goal, four quantified objectives, and named users (GBRMPA, CSIRO/universities, BoM) with needs explicitly traced to objectives. Well referenced throughout. Minor issue: 344,400 km² is the Marine Park area, not reef area, and the objectives are not fully justified quantitatively.

evidence.quote: Give reef managers direct, repeatable observations of coral colour over the whole Great Barrier Reef
Objectives 1 and 3 come directly from the managers' need to react within days

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Gantt chart with status colours, task descriptions, logical dependency ordering, and a risk/contingency table with triggers and responses. Information sources are listed with purposes. The plan is tied to the mission narrative. Slightly less detail on launch-stage milestones.

evidence.quote: the imaging requirements (objectives 1 and 2) fix the orbit altitude and local time, so orbit work comes before ground control
No single orbit meets weekly coverage at 10 m

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Hand calculations for period, orbits per day, sun-synchronous inclination, ground-track shift and swath are correct and checked against STK. Results are interpreted to expose a real coverage trade-off. Launch-stage progress is absent, and the 6,000-pixel sensor assumption is unjustified.

evidence.quote: Weekly coverage (objective 1) is therefore not guaranteed by one satellite at this altitude and resolution.
Ground-track shift per orbit at the equator | 360° × T / 86,164 s | 24.2° ≈ 2,700 km

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Logical headed structure, labelled figures and tables, consistent formatting, and all 11 references appear in text and list. Some weaknesses: reference [11] is a weak source, and the deadline markers on the Gantt chart are barely visible.

evidence.quote: Figure 1: Project Gantt chart, Weeks 2 to 10 (gold = completed, blue = planned, red lines = report deadlines).
[11] "Monitoring coral reefs from space," ResearchGate publication 231179724.

technical_issues.issue: 344,400 km² is the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park area, not the reef's area; the figure should be attributed correctly or reworded.
The 6,000-pixel across-track count used for the 60 km swath is an assumed sensor size that is not justified or linked to a stated detector.
R2 asks for launch to be applied, but launch vehicles and trajectories are not analysed in the preliminary work; only orbit is addressed.

overall: A strong, well-structured preliminary report with a clear mission concept, a robust Gantt-based plan with contingencies, and correct orbit calculations that expose a real coverage trade-off. Main gaps are the absence of launch analysis, an unjustified sensor assumption, and a misattributed reef area figure.

feedback.summary: You have produced a strong, well-structured preliminary report. Your mission concept is clear, with four quantified objectives and named users whose needs are traced to those objectives. Your Gantt-based plan, with a risk and contingency table, and your orbit calculations, which expose a real coverage trade-off, show good technical progress. Remaining gaps are the missing launch analysis, an unjustified sensor assumption, and one misattributed area figure.
next_steps: Correct the 344,400 km² figure so it is attributed to the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park rather than the reef itself, or reword it.
Justify the 6,000-pixel across-track count by linking it to a named detector or sensor specification, and state the source.
Add a preliminary launch analysis covering candidate launch vehicles and the resulting trajectory, so the work meets the launch requirement (R2) as well as the orbit analysis.

criteria.C1: You set out a clear goal, four quantified objectives, and named users (GBRMPA, CSIRO/universities, BoM), with needs explicitly linked to objectives, and your referencing is strong. To reach the top band, quantitatively justify the objectives and correct the reef area figure, which is the Marine Park area rather than the reef's area.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart, task descriptions, logical dependency ordering, and risk table with triggers and responses make the plan robust, and you explain why the plan follows the mission narrative (for example, orbit work before ground control). To reach the top band, add a little more detail on launch-stage milestones.
criteria.C3: Your hand calculations for period, orbits per day, inclination, ground-track shift and swath are correct and checked against STK, and you interpret them well. To strengthen this, show progress on the launch stage and justify the sensor pixel assumption.
criteria.C4: Your report has a logical headed structure, labelled figures and tables, and all 11 references are cited in text and listed. To improve, replace the weak source [11] with a more authoritative reference and make the Gantt deadline markers clearly visible.
